component.name: OpenEmux
component.summary: Browse and play your retro game library

description.p: OpenEmux is a clean, GNOME-native frontend that makes RetroArch simple and enjoyable: add, browse and organize your retro game library by console and, with a compatible gamepad, play the games you already own. It was inspired by OpenEmu, bringing that same polished experience to Linux.

OpenEmux runs games through RetroArch, so the RetroArch Flatpak must be installed and its cores downloaded (via RetroArch's own Online Updater). Install it with: flatpak install flathub org.libretro.RetroArch
OpenEmux ships no games, ROMs or BIOS files. Use only content you legally own. Emulation matters for preserving the history and culture of video games — please respect the people who created them.
Features:

ul.li: A cover-art library organized by console, with favorites
Per-console keyboard and gamepad mappings
Per-console video shaders
BIOS status checks and cover-art syncing

description.p: OpenEmux runs on distributions that are not Debian-derived: the AppImage starts, and it can reach the network.

ul.li: The AppImage starts on Arch and on any distribution whose shell is newer than the bundle's libraries
HTTPS works everywhere: the bundle trusts the machine's own certificate store, so first-time setup finishes
"Open folder", the RetroArch Flatpak probe and the audio probe are no longer handed the bundle's environment
Every packaged icon is exactly the size its directory claims, with the small sizes desktops ask for
A native Arch Linux package, built and install-tested like every other format
Tamil is available as an interface language

description.p: The library becomes the user's own: it remembers where it was left, it groups what it shows, and the consoles sit in the order the user puts them in.

ul.li: "Favorites" is in the sidebar only while something is favorited, appearing with the first star and going with the last
The library reopens on the view it was closed on, stored in a small session file of its own
"All", "Favorites" and the collections group their games by console, each group under its own header and count
The cartridge shelf works on those pages: every group is drawn in its own console's frame, with per-ROM cartridge colours
Consoles can be reordered by dragging a sidebar row, with Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down, or from Preferences
A console with no games right now keeps its place in the arrangement for when it comes back

description.p: OpenEmux arrives on Windows and on ARM, and the library it manages is faster and safer than it has ever been.

ul.li: Windows is a supported platform: an installer, a portable bundle, gamepads read through SDL2 and RetroArch shipped alongside
Every Linux format is now built for aarch64 as well as x86_64
The grid builds a screenful instead of the whole collection, and stops re-reading, re-hashing and re-decoding work it had already done
Persistence is atomic: settings, playlists and favorites are written whole or not at all, and a corrupt file is kept instead of being replaced with defaults
Favorites survive a drive that is not mounted, and first boot works offline by falling back to the bundled cores
Sign in to RetroAchievements once and unlock achievements on every launch
Export and import saves and save states from one place
Advanced core settings for PlayStation and PSP, and the option to import ROMs as links instead of copies
Shader packs can no longer write outside the shader directory
The AppImage no longer needs libfuse2, and every package ships the metadata software centres read

description.p: The game window never strands a game any more.

ul.li: When the game window cannot take over RetroArch, the game is reopened in its own decorated window instead of being left as an undecorated square that cannot be moved, resized or fullscreened
The window now shows what it is doing while the game starts, and gives up in seconds instead of after twenty silent ones
RetroArch is kept on X11 while embedding, so the window can actually be adopted on Wayland desktops
A gamepad's fullscreen button can no longer break a working embed

description.p: A game's settings stay with the game.

ul.li: Stop writing per-launch settings into the user's own RetroArch configuration, which left borderless windows, an unbound fullscreen hotkey and OpenEmux's save-state directory behind for good
Give RetroArch its decorated window back when the OpenEmux game window is off, healing a configuration an earlier version already changed
Find the host's audio server on Flatpak installs, so games no longer run at the monitor's refresh rate with no sound

description.p: Closing a game now really ends it.

ul.li: Closing the game window stops the emulator instead of leaving it running with no window, audible and reachable only from a process manager
Closing the library window ends a running game with it, so no game outlives the app

description.p: Games now play inside OpenEmux, and artwork finds itself.

ul.li: Play in an OpenEmux game window that hosts the running emulator, with pause, reset, save and load state, volume and input settings in its header bar
Ship a local database of 60,600 game names, so cover lookup resolves real titles instead of guessing URLs
Ask the cover picker for suggestions by name, including approximate matches for misspelled queries
Sync covers in parallel and reveal each one as it lands, instead of only when the whole run finishes
Carry save states, battery saves and artwork with a ROM when it is renamed
Choose System, Light or Dark in Settings, or flip the theme from the header bar
Open a console's controller settings from its context menu in the sidebar

description.p: A fix for the all-Flatpak setup: games launch again.

ul.li: Grant the sandbox read access to the RetroArch Flatpak's cores, which --filesystem=home does not cover; without it every launch failed with "No RetroArch core found"

description.p: A fix for games running far too fast outside the Flatpak.

ul.li: Hand RetroArch an audio driver it actually has, so audio starts and the emulation runs at the right speed

description.p: Controls you can actually configure, and changes that reach the running game.

ul.li: A remap saved mid-game now applies immediately, keeping your progress
A connected gamepad and the keyboard are configured together, not either/or
Analog deadzone and sensitivity, rumble, latency and the rest of the input knobs
Choose which controller the core is told is plugged in, per console
The missing system hotkeys, including disk control for multi-disc games
Play the left analog stick from the keyboard, and let a pad's D-pad move it
Every symbolic icon ships with the app, so none go missing on any desktop
Missing artwork is now visible and recoverable, and covers decode off the main thread

description.p: The artwork Import tab, finished: it missed the 1.9.1 build.

ul.li: An imported image gets the whole area, with a trash button to clear it
The import controls and the save destination share a single row

description.p: Fixes for the ROM artwork actions, and a friendlier artwork manager.

ul.li: Fix a crash when acting on a ROM's context menu
Sync one ROM's cover or label from the menu, in the background
Open the artwork manager from its own "Manage cover/label" entries
Show search results on the library's grid, and mark the picked image
Cancel a running artwork search
Give an imported image the whole area, with one row of edit controls

description.p: Personalise the shelf, act on many games at once, and take control of the running game.

ul.li: Pick a cartridge shell colour per game, from a palette of twelve
Select several ROMs with Shift/Ctrl, the keyboard, or a gamepad selection mode
Manage artwork per ROM: search every provider by name or hash, or import and edit your own
Order and switch the artwork providers, with OpenEmux's own mirror as a new source
Adjust the running game's volume, and start a game from any save-state slot
Fold the analog stick onto the D-pad, and map a turbo/autofire modifier
OpenEmux now ships as a Flatpak

description.p: ScreenScraper out of the box, cartridge labels, and per-ROM overrides.

ul.li: ScreenScraper works with no account: official builds embed a developer credential
Cartridge labels are scraped into their own folder and composited into the cartridge art
Per-ROM core and shader overrides from the context menu

description.p: The core, the shader, the layout and the grouping, all chosen from the interface.

ul.li: Choose the shader per ROM from the context menu, over the per-console setting
Choose the libretro core per console (Settings) and per ROM (context menu)
Configure the library layout (view mode, sort, zoom) per console and per view
Group games into custom collections in the sidebar, spanning consoles

description.p: Three layouts, six sort orders and a zoom control, one click from the toolbar.

ul.li: A View Mode selector: cover grid, cartridge grid and a compact list
Zoom controls for thumbnails (50%-200%), with Ctrl+plus/minus/0
Sort the library by name, recently played, recently added, size or platform
Follow the desktop language on first launch instead of defaulting to English
Open the primary menu from the gamepad, and steer with the right analog stick

description.p: A fix for the AppImage, where no cartridge or cover art rendered at all.

ul.li: Fix cartridge frames and cover art not rendering in the AppImage
Degrade to the plain cover when a cartridge cannot be composited

description.p: A fix for the 1.5.0 AppImage, which did not start at all.

ul.li: Fix the AppImage failing to start with "usr/bin/python3: not found"

description.p: The whole library, navigable with a gamepad or the keyboard.

ul.li: Navigate the whole library with a gamepad, following the RetroArch button convention
Full keyboard navigation, with shortcuts for play, rename, delete, favorite, rescan, import and cover sync
Show what each control does in the bottom bar, per input device
Lay the game grid out like an icon view, with fixed card sizes per console
Fix the launcher picking a python3 without PyGObject (pyenv/conda/asdf)

description.p: Cartridge artwork, and managing ROMs from the library.

ul.li: Every game is shown inside its console's cartridge, composed from vector artwork and cached; nine consoles are covered and the look is on by default
The favorite star on a cover is a button now, so favoriting is one click
Rename a ROM from its context menu: the file, its artwork and the playlists all follow
Delete a ROM from its context menu; the file goes to the system trash, where it can be restored
Select several ROMs by dragging across the library, then delete them or sync covers for just those

description.p: Context menu fixes and discoverability.

ul.li: The sidebar context menu stays open instead of closing as soon as the mouse button is released
Context menu entries now show an icon
A three-dot button on ROM covers and sidebar consoles opens the context menu with a plain click
The favorite star moved to the top-left corner of the cover

description.p: ROM import, archive support and controller mapping.

ul.li: ROMs inside .zip archives are recognized; archives are extracted for cores that need a real file
Import ROMs from the main window, by button or drag and drop
Map controls by pressing the buttons on the controller, with up to four gamepad ports
Optional ScreenScraper cover source, including cartridge label art
Rotating tips status bar and a rebindable fullscreen toggle
Cover sync can be stopped while it runs

description.p: Library and packaging update.

ul.li: Per-console cover proportions and a separate cartridge-label image slot
Redesigned "All" library view with per-game console labels
Background check for new releases on startup
Native .deb and .rpm packages alongside the AppImage

description.p: Maintenance release.

ul.li: Cached cartridge textures and smaller frame assets
Documentation and website updates

description.p: First Flatpak release.

ul.li: Plays games through the RetroArch Flatpak
Renamed to OpenEmux for naming consistency

description.p: First stable release.

ul.li: GNOME HIG interface built on libadwaita
Cover-art library, per-console input and shaders, BIOS checks
